nodes.statement: We discuss the relationship between the two-set policy in this paper and a policy from prior work named the set-expansion policy citepHonXieCheWan_24. The set-expansion policy achieves an O(1/sqrtN) optimality gap under the aperiodic unichain assumption (Crefassump:aperiodic-unichain); it works by letting arms in a specific subset follow sysbarpi^* and gradually expanding the subset. The two-set policy in this paper refines this approach by maintaining two judiciously chosen sets instead of one set. Furthermore, we argue that the two-set policy can be implemented in a way such that when Assumption~ or fails, it achieves O(1/sqrtN) optimality gap, because it becomes almost the same as the set-expansion policy. To see this, note that when Assumption~ (non-degeneracy) fails, it holds that eta = 0; when Assumption~ (local stability) fails, the matrix U becomes infinity; in either case, D^textupOL_t = emptyset. By taking suitable actions for the arms in (D^textupOL_tcup D^sysbarpi^*_t)^c, we can maintain a subset of arms following the Unconstrained Optimal Control that gradually expands in the same way as the set-expansion policy. Using similar arguments as those in , one can prove an O(1/sqrtN) bound for the two-set policy.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{remark:two-set-one-set}
We discuss the relationship between the two-set policy in this paper and a policy from prior work named the set-expansion policy \citep{HonXieCheWan_24}. The set-expansion policy achieves an $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ optimality gap under the aperiodic unichain assumption (\Cref{assump:aperiodic-unichain}); it works by letting arms in a specific subset follow ${{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}$ and gradually expanding the subset. 
The two-set policy in this paper refines this approach by maintaining two judiciously chosen sets instead of one set. 
Furthermore, we argue that the two-set policy can be implemented in a way such that when Assumption~\ref{assump:non-degeneracy} or \ref{assump:local-stability} fails, it achieves $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ optimality gap, because it becomes almost the same as the set-expansion policy. 
To see this, note that when Assumption~\ref{assump:non-degeneracy} (non-degeneracy) fails, it holds that $\eta = 0$; when Assumption~\ref{assump:local-stability} (local stability) fails, the matrix $U$ becomes infinity; in either case, $D^{\textup{OL}}_t = \emptyset$. 
By taking suitable actions for the arms in $(D^{\textup{OL}}_t\cup D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t)^c$, we can maintain a subset of arms following the Unconstrained Optimal Control that gradually expands in the same way as the set-expansion policy. 
Using similar arguments as those in \cite{HonXieCheWan_24}, one can prove an $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ bound for the two-set policy.

The two-set policy in this paper refines this approach by maintaining two judiciously chosen sets instead of one set. Furthermore, we argue that the two-set policy can be implemented in a way such that when Assumption~ or fails, it achieves O(1/sqrtN) optimality gap, because it becomes almost the same as the set-expansion policy. To see this, note that when Assumption~ (non-degeneracy) fails, it holds that eta = 0; when Assumption~ (local stability) fails, the matrix U becomes infinity; in either case, D^textupOL_t = emptyset. By taking suitable actions for the arms in (D^textupOL_tcup D^sysbarpi^*_t)^c, we can maintain a subset of arms following the Unconstrained Optimal Control that gradually expands in the same way as the set-expansion policy. Using similar arguments as those in , one can prove an O(1/sqrtN) bound for the two-set policy.

nodes.statement: The proof of Crefthm:instability-lower-bound is based on the following idea: By Creflem:opt-gap-linear-comp, arms need to closely follow the Optimal Local Control to maintain a small optimality gap; however, if the Optimal Local Control is locally unstable, the system will quickly drift away from the region where the Optimal Local Control is applicable. In the proof, we use Lyapunov functions to quantify how much the system drifts away from mu^* in each step, based on how closely it follows the Optimal Local Control. We prove the following in Crefapp:locally-unstable-example by giving a concrete example of regular unstable RB. corollaryexistregularunstable There exists an RB satisfying Assumptions and and violating Crefassump:local-stability such that R^textuprel - R(pi, veS_0) geq OmegaBig(frac1sqrtNBig).

nodes.statement: By definition, if all N arms follow Unconstrained Optimal Control at time t, the expected number of arms in state s taking action a is equal to X_t([N], s)sysbarpi^*(a|s). Among these arms, the fraction of arms transitioning to state s' in the next time step equals P(s,a,s'). Since the state transition of each arm is Markovian given the state and action, the expected number of arms going from state s to state s' and taking action a equals X_t([N], s)sysbarpi^*(a|s)P(s,a,s'). Summing over s and a, we get &mspace23mu EX_t+1([N], s') \,|\, X_t, textupall arms follow Crefalg:follow-pibs \\ &= sum_sinS, ainA X_t([N], s)sysbarpi^*(a|s)P(s,a,s') forall s'inS, which completes the proof of the lemma.

Throughout this proof, we use the shorthand $x$ for $x([N])$, and omit ``$\ve{A}_t\sim \textup{Optimal Local Control}$'' in the conditioning. 

We fixed an arbitrary $x$ and let $X_t = x$.  
For any $s\neq \tilde{s}$ and $a\in\mathbb{A}$, the expected number of arms taking action $a$ equals $x(s) {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(a|s)$; for $s=\tilde{s}$, the expected number of arms taking action $1$ equals $\alpha -\sum_{s\neq\tilde{s} }x(s){{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s)$. and the expected number of arms taking action $0$ equals $1-\alpha- \sum_{s\neq\tilde{s} }x(s){{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(0|s)$. 
Therefore, 
for any $s'\in\mathbb{S}$ such that $s'\neq \tilde{s}$, 
\begin{align}
    &\E{X_{t+1}(s') \,|\, X_t=x} \nonumber \\
    \nonumber
    &= \sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}, a\in\mathbb{A}} x(s) {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(a|s) P(s,a,s') \\ 
    \nonumber
    &\mspace{20mu} + \Big(\alpha - \sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}} x(s){{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s)\Big) P(\tilde{s}, 1, s') 
    \nonumber
    + \Big(1 - \alpha - \sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}} x(s) {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(0|s) \Big) P(\tilde{s}, 0, s')  \\
    \nonumber
    &= \sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}} x(s)P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(s, s')
    + \Big(\alpha - \sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}} x(s) {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s)\Big)P_1(\tilde{s}, s') 
    + \Big(1 - \alpha - \sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}} x(s){{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(0|s) \Big)P_0(\tilde{s}, s') \\
    \label{eq:derive-phi-1}
    &= \sum_{s\in\mathbb{S}} x(s)P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(s,s')  - x(\tilde{s})P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(\tilde{s}, s')  \\
    \nonumber
    &\mspace{20mu} + \Big(\alpha - \sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}} x(s) {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s)\Big)P_1(\tilde{s}, s') 
    + \Big(1 - \alpha - \sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}} x(s){{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(0|s) \Big)P_0(\tilde{s}, s'). 
\end{align}
Because $P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(\tilde{s},s') =  {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|\tilde{s}) P_1(\tilde{s},s')+ {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(0|\tilde{s})P_0(\tilde{s}, s')$, we expand the second term in \eqref{eq:derive-phi-1} and rearrange the terms to get
\begin{align}
    &\mspace{20mu} \E{X_{t+1}(s') \,|\, X_t=x} \nonumber\\
    &=  \sum_{s\in\mathbb{S}} x(s)P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(s,s')
    +  \Big(\alpha - \sum_{s\in\mathbb{S}} x(s) {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s) \Big) P_1(\tilde{s}, s')
    + \Big(1 - \alpha - \sum_{s\in\mathbb{S}} x(s) {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(0|s) \Big) P_0(\tilde{s}, s')\nonumber \\
    &= \sum_{s\in\mathbb{S}} x(s) P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(s,s') 
    + \Big(\alpha - \sum_{s\in\mathbb{S}} x(s){{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s) \Big) P_1(\tilde{s}, s')
    -\Big(  \alpha - \sum_{s\in\mathbb{S}} x(s){{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s) \Big) P_0(\tilde{s}, s') \label{eq:derive-phi-2}\\
    &= \sum_{s\in\mathbb{S}} x(s)\Big(P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(s,s') -  {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s)\big(P_1(\tilde{s}, s') - P_0(\tilde{s}, s')\big) \Big) + \alpha (P_1(\tilde{s}, s') - P_0(\tilde{s}, s')),  \label{eq:derive-phi-3}
\end{align}
where \eqref{eq:derive-phi-2} uses the facts that ${{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(0|s) = 1-{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s)$ and $\sum_{s\in\mathbb{S}} x(s) = 1$. 

Next, we calculate $\E{X_{t+1}(\tilde{s}) \,|\, X_t=x}$. 
Observe that $X_{t+1}(\tilde{s}) = 1 - \sum_{s'\neq \tilde{s}} X_{t+1}(s')$, so
\begin{align}
    \nonumber
    &\mspace{20mu} \E{X_{t+1}(\tilde{s}) \,|\, X_t=x}\\
    \nonumber
    &= 1 - \sum_{s'\neq \tilde{s}} \E{X_{t+1}(s') \,|\, X_t=x} \nonumber \\
    \nonumber
    &= \sum_{s\in\mathbb{S}}  x(s)\Big(1 - \sum_{s'\neq \tilde{s}} P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(s,s') + \sum_{s'\neq\tilde{s}}  {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s) \big(P_1(\tilde{s}, s') - P_0(\tilde{s}, s')\big) \Big) - \alpha \sum_{s'\neq\tilde{s}}(P_1(\tilde{s}, s') - P_0(\tilde{s}, s')) \\
    \label{eq:derive-phi-3-sneu}
    &= \sum_{s\in\mathbb{S}} x(s) \Big(P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(s,\tilde{s}) -  {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s) \big(P_1(\tilde{s}, \tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s}, \tilde{s})\big)\Big)  + \alpha (P_1(\tilde{s}, \tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s}, \tilde{s})).
\end{align}
Note that \eqref{eq:derive-phi-3-sneu} has the same form as \eqref{eq:derive-phi-3}, with $s'$ replaced by $\tilde{s}$. 

We rewrite \eqref{eq:derive-phi-3} and \eqref{eq:derive-phi-3-sneu} in matrix form to get 
\begin{align}\label{eq:derive-phi-4}
    \E{X_{t+1} \,|\, X_t=x} 
    &= x\Big(P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*} - c_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}^\top \big(P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})\big) \Big) + \alpha (P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})).
\end{align}
Recall that we have let $\Phi = P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*} - \mathbbm{1}^\top \mu^* - (c_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*} - \alpha \mathbbm{1})^\top \big(P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})\big)$, we can verify that the RHS of \eqref{eq:derive-phi-4} is the same as $(x-\mu^*)\Phi + \mu^*$. Specifically, 
\begin{align}
    (x-\mu^*)\Phi + \mu^* 
    \nonumber
    &= (x-\mu^*)\Big(P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*} - \mathbbm{1}^\top \mu^* - (c_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*} - \alpha \mathbbm{1})^\top \big(P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})\big)\Big) + \mu^* \\
    \nonumber
    &= x \Big(P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*} - c_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}^\top \big(P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})\big) \Big) + x\Big(- \mathbbm{1}^\top \mu^* -  \alpha \mathbbm{1}^\top \big(P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})\big)\Big) \\
    \nonumber
    &\mspace{20mu} - \mu^* \Big(P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*} - c_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}^\top \big(P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})\big) \Big) - \mu^* \Big(- \mathbbm{1}^\top \mu^* -  \alpha \mathbbm{1}^\top \big(P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})\big)\Big) + \mu^*\\
    \nonumber
    &= x \Big(P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*} - c_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}^\top \big(P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})\big) \Big) - \mu^* - \alpha \big(P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})\big) \\
    \label{eq:derive-phi-5}
    &\mspace{20mu} - \mu^*  + \alpha \big(P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})\big) +  \mu^* +  \alpha \big(P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})\big) + \mu^* \\
    \nonumber
    &= x\Big(P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*} - c_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}^\top \big(P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})\big) \Big) + \alpha (P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})). 
\end{align}
where to get \eqref{eq:derive-phi-5} we use the facts that $x\mathbbm{1}^\top = \mu^* \mathbbm{1}^\top = 1$ and $\mu^* c_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}^\top = \alpha$. 
Substituting the RHS of \eqref{eq:derive-phi-4}  with $(x-\mu^*)\Phi + \mu^*$, we have proved that under the Optimal Local Control, $\E{X_{t+1} \,|\, X_t=x} = (x-\mu^*)\Phi + \mu^*$. 
This completes the proof of \Cref{lem:lp-priority-and-phi}.

nodes.statement: We first argue that the arms in D^textupOL_t can follow the Optimal Local Control. By the definition of D^textupOL_t, if D^textupOL_t neq emptyset, then delta(X_t, D^textupOL_t) geq 0. Because (eta, epsilon_N^fe) is feasibility ensuring, holds for the arms in D^textupOL_t, i.e., sum_sneq tildes sysbarpi^*(1|s) X_t(D^textupOL_t, s) &leq alpha m(D^textupOL_t) - frac|S^emptyset|+1N, \\ sum_sneq tildes sysbarpi^*(0|s) X_t(D^textupOL_t, s) &leq (1-alpha)m(D^textupOL_t) - frac|S^emptyset|+1N. which allows these arms to follow the Optimal Local Control. It remains to show that A_t(i) for inotin D^textupOL_t cup D^sysbarpi^*_t can be chosen such that sum_iin[N] A_t(i) = alpha N, if the arms in D^textupOL_t and D^sysbarpi^*_t follow the Optimal Local Control and the Unconstrained Optimal Control, respectively. By the definition of the Optimal Local Control, sum_iin D^textupOL_t A_t(i) in \lflooralpha |D^textupOL_t|rfloor, lceilalpha |D^textupOL_t|rceil\. Because A_t(i)in \0,1\ for iin D^sysbarpi^*_t, we have \[ flooralpha |D^textupOL_t| leq sum_iin D^textupOL_tcup D^sysbarpi^*_t A_t(i)leq ceilalpha |D^textupOL_t| + |D^sysbarpi^*_t|. \] Because we can choose sum_inotin D^textupOL_tcup D^sysbarpi^*_t A_t(i) to be anything integer between 0 and N - |D^textupOL_t| - |D^sysbarpi^*_t| to satisfy the budget constraint, it suffices to show that flooralpha |D^textupOL_t| + (N - |D^textupOL_t| - |D^sysbarpi^*_t|) &geq alpha N \\ ceilalpha |D^textupOL_t| + |D^sysbarpi^*_t| &leq alpha N. To show , observe that |D^sysbarpi^*_t| = biglfloor beta (N -|D^textupOL_t|)bigrfloor leq (1-alpha)(N - |D^textupOL_t|), so alpha |D^textupOL_t| + (N - |D^textupOL_t| - |D^sysbarpi^*_t|) geq alpha N. Rounding both sides down to the nearest integers, and utilizing the fact that N - |D^textupOL_t| - |D^sysbarpi^*_t| and alpha N are integers, we get . Similarly, to show , observe that |D^sysbarpi^*_t| leq alpha (N - |D^textupOL_t|), so \[ alpha |D^textupOL_t| + |D^sysbarpi^*_t| leq alpha N. \] Rounding both sides up to the nearest integers, we get .

Therefore, it remains to bound Probdelta(X_t+1, D^textupOL_t) < 0 \,big|\, Sigma_t. Recall that delta(x, D) = eta m(D) - normplainx(D)- m(D) mu^*_U - epsilon_N^fe = eta m(D) - h_U(x, D) - epsilon_N^fe, so nonumber Probdelta(X_t+1, D^textupOL_t) < 0 \,big|\, Sigma_t &= Probh_U(X_t+1,D^textupOL_t) > eta m(D^textupOL_t) -epsilon_N^fe \,big|\, Sigma_t, When D^textupOL_t neq emptyset, we have delta(X_t, D^textupOL_t) geq 0, implying h_U(X_t, D^textupOL_t) leq eta m(D^textupOL_t) - epsilon_N^fe. If m(D^sysbarpi^*_t) leq epsilon_N^rd, \[ beta(1-m(D^textupOL_t)) - frac1N leq m(D^sysbarpi^*_t) leq epsilon_N^rd, \] which implies by the non-negativity of h_W(X_t, D^sysbarpi^*_t). If m(D^sysbarpi^*_t) > epsilon_N^rd, holds. Because m(D^sysbarpi^*_t) = floorbeta (N - |D^textupOL_t|) /N geq big(beta (N - |D^textupOL_t|) - 1big) / N, we have lambda_U^1/2 h_W(X_t, D^sysbarpi^*_t) &> eta big(beta(N -|D^textupOL_t|)-1big)frac1N - epsilon_N^rd - epsilon_N^fe \\ &= eta beta(1-m(D^textupOL_t)) - fracetaN - epsilon_N^rd - epsilon_N^fe, which implies after rearranging the terms. Because normv_U leq lambda_U^1/2normv_2 leq lambda_U^1/2normv_W for any vin R^|S|, nonumber normbigX_t(D^sysbarpi^*_t) - m(D^sysbarpi^*_t) mu^*_U &leq lambda_U^1/2normbigX_t(D^sysbarpi^*_t) - m(D^sysbarpi^*_t) mu^*_W leq eta m(D^sysbarpi^*_t) - epsilon_N^rd - epsilon_N^fe. Observe that \eqref{eq:two-set:sufficient-coverage:goal-2} follows directly from the definition of the policy, so we only need to prove \eqref{eq:two-set:sufficient-coverage:goal-1}. 
    We claim that either $m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) \leq \epsilon_N^{\text{rd}}$, or 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:two-set:sufficient-coverage:interm-goal-1}
        \lambda_U^{1/2} h_W(X_t, D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) >  \eta m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) - \epsilon_N^{\text{rd}} - \epsilon_N^{\text{fe}}. 
    \end{equation}
    We first show \eqref{eq:two-set:sufficient-coverage:goal-1} assuming this claim. 
    Recall that $m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_{t})= \big\lfloor \beta (N -|D^{\textup{OL}}_{t}|)\big\rfloor \big/ N$. If $m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) \leq \epsilon_N^{\text{rd}}$, 
    \[
        \beta(1-m(D^{\textup{OL}}_t)) - \frac{1}{N} \leq m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) \leq \epsilon_N^{\text{rd}},
    \]
    which implies \eqref{eq:two-set:sufficient-coverage:goal-1} by the non-negativity of $h_W(X_t, D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t)$. 
    If $m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) > \epsilon_N^{\text{rd}}$, \eqref{eq:two-set:sufficient-coverage:interm-goal-1} holds. Because $m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) = \floor{\beta (N - |D^{\textup{OL}}_t|)} /N \geq \big(\beta (N - |D^{\textup{OL}}_t|) - 1\big) / N$, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \lambda_U^{1/2} h_W(X_t, D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) &>  \eta \big(\beta(N -|D^{\textup{OL}}_{t}|)-1\big)\frac{1}{N} -  \epsilon_N^{\text{rd}} - \epsilon_N^{\text{fe}} \\
        &=  \eta \beta(1-m(D^{\textup{OL}}_t)) -  \frac{\eta}{N} - \epsilon_N^{\text{rd}} - \epsilon_N^{\text{fe}},
    \end{align*}
    which implies \eqref{eq:two-set:sufficient-coverage:goal-1} after rearranging the terms. 

    Now we prove the claim by contradiction. Suppose, at a certain time $t$, we have $m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) > \epsilon_N^{\text{rd}}$ and $ \lambda_U^{1/2}h_W(X_t, D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) \leq \eta m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) - \epsilon_N^{\text{rd}} - \epsilon_N^{\text{fe}}$. Because $\norm{v}_U \leq \lambda_U^{1/2}\norm{v}_2 \leq \lambda_U^{1/2}\norm{v}_W$ for any $v\in \mathbb{R}^{|\mathbb{S}|}$, 
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
        \normbig{X_t(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) - m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) \mu^*}_U 
        &\leq \lambda_U^{1/2}\normbig{X_t(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) - m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) \mu^*}_W
        \leq  \eta m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) - \epsilon_N^{\text{rd}} - \epsilon_N^{\text{fe}}. 
    \end{align}
    Combined with the triangular inequality and the definition of $D^{\textup{OL}}_t$, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \normbig{X_t(D^{\textup{OL}}_t\cup D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) - m(D^{\textup{OL}}_t\cup D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) \mu^*}_U &\leq \normbig{X_t(D^{\textup{OL}}_t) - m(D^{\textup{OL}}_t) \mu^*}_U  + \normbig{X_t(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) - m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) \mu^*}_U \\
        &\leq \eta m(D^{\textup{OL}}_t) + \eta m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) - \epsilon_N^{\text{rd}} - \epsilon_N^{\text{fe}}.
    \end{align*}
    Consequently, $D^{\textup{OL}}_t\cup D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t$ is a superset of $D^{\textup{OL}}_t$ such that $\delta(X_t, D^{\textup{OL}}_t\cup D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) \geq \epsilon_N^{\text{rd}}$ and $m(D^{\textup{OL}}_t \cup D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) = m(D^{\textup{OL}}_t) + m(D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t) > m(D^{\textup{OL}}_t) + \epsilon_N^{\text{rd}}$, contradicting the $\epsilon_N^{\text{rd}}$-maximality of $D^{\textup{OL}}_t$. 
    We have thus proved the claim that implies  \eqref{eq:two-set:sufficient-coverage:goal-1}.

nodes.statement: We will first bound the norm of the long-run expectation of the X_t([N]) - mu^* using ProbbigD^textupOL_infty neq [N], and then derive the optimality gap bound. Let Q = (I - Phi)^-1, which is well-defined because all eigenvalues of Phi have moduli strictly less than 1 (Crefassump:local-stability). By direct calculation, we have that for any vinDelta(S), (v - mu^*) Q - (v - mu^*)Phi Q = v - mu^*. We will first bound the norm of the long-run expectation of the $X_t([N]) - \mu^*$ using $\Probbig{D^{\textup{OL}}_\infty \neq [N]}$, and then derive the optimality gap bound. 
    
    Let $Q = (I - \Phi)^{-1}$, which is well-defined because all eigenvalues of $\Phi$ have moduli strictly less than $1$ (\Cref{assump:local-stability}). 
    By direct calculation, we have that for any $v\in\Delta(\mathbb{S})$,
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:phi-stein-equation}
        (v - \mu^*) Q - (v - \mu^*)\Phi Q = v - \mu^*. 
    \end{equation}
    We define the positive constant $\lambda_{Q}$ as
    \[
        \lambda_{Q} = \max\Big\{\max_{v\in\Delta(\mathbb{S})} \norm{(v-\mu^*) Q}_1,  \max_{v\in\Delta(\mathbb{S})} \norm{(v-\mu^*) \Phi Q}_1\Big\},
    \]
    which must be finite because $\Delta(\mathbb{S})$ is a compact set.
    
    
    Letting $v = X_t([N])$ and taking the expectation (for random vectors) in \eqref{eq:phi-stein-equation}, we get
    \begin{align}
        \Ebig{X_t([N]) - \mu^*}
        \nonumber
        &= \Ebig{(X_t([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi Q} \\
        \nonumber
        &= \Ebig{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi Q} \\
        \nonumber
        &\mspace{20mu} - \Ebig{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N])-\mu^*)Q}.
    \end{align}
    Using the fact that 
    \[
         \lim_{T\to\infty} \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \Ebig{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N])-\mu^*)Q} = 0,  
    \]
    we get 
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:two-set:state-diff-steins-diff}
        \lim_{T\to\infty} \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \Ebig{X_t([N]) - \mu^*} = \lim_{T\to\infty} \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \Ebig{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi Q}.
    \end{equation} 
    Theerefore, it remains to bound $\Ebig{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi Q}$ for every time step $t$. 
    
    Let $\Sigma_t = (X_t, D^{\textup{OL}}_t, D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t)$. 
    We will bound $\Ebig{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N]-\mu^*)\Phi Q \,\big|\, \Sigma_t}$ by decomposing it into two terms: 
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
        &\mspace{20mu} \Ebig{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi Q \,\big|\, \Sigma_t} \\
        \label{eq:steins-difference-lp-is-N}
        &= \Ebig{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi Q  \,\big|\, \Sigma_t} \indibrac{D^{\textup{OL}}_t = [N]}\\
        \label{eq:steins-difference-lp-not-N}
        &\mspace{20mu} + \Ebig{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi Q  \,\big|\, \Sigma_t} \indibrac{D^{\textup{OL}}_t \neq [N]}.
    \end{align}
    For the term in \eqref{eq:steins-difference-lp-is-N}, note that by \Cref{lem:lp-priority-and-phi}, $\Ebig{X_{t+1}([N]) -\mu^* \,\big|\, \Sigma_t} = (X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi$ when $D^{\textup{OL}}_t = [N]$, so 
    \begin{equation*}
        \Ebig{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q \,\big|\, \Sigma_t}  \indibrac{D^{\textup{OL}}_t = [N]}  
        = (X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi Q \indibrac{D^{\textup{OL}}_t = [N]}, 
    \end{equation*}
    which implies that the term in \eqref{eq:steins-difference-lp-is-N} is zero. For the term in \eqref{eq:steins-difference-lp-not-N}, its $L_1$ norm can be bounded as 
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
         &\mspace{20mu} \norm{\Ebig{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi Q  \,\big|\, \Sigma_t}}_1 \indibrac{D^{\textup{OL}}_t \neq [N]} \\
         \nonumber
         &\leq  \Ebig{\norm{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi Q}_1  \,\big|\, \Sigma_t} \indibrac{D^{\textup{OL}}_t \neq [N]} \\
         \nonumber
         &\leq \Ebig{\norm{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q}_1 + \norm{(X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi Q}_1  \,\big|\, \Sigma_t} \indibrac{D^{\textup{OL}}_t \neq [N]}  \\
         \label{eq:steins-difference-bound-by-lamq}
        &\leq 2\lambda_{Q} \indibrac{D^{\textup{OL}}_t \neq [N]},
    \end{align}
    where \eqref{eq:steins-difference-bound-by-lamq} follows from the definition of $\lambda_{Q}$ and the fact that $X_{t+1}([N]), X_t([N]) \in \Delta(\mathbb{S})$. 
    Combining the calculations of the two terms in \eqref{eq:steins-difference-lp-is-N} and \eqref{eq:steins-difference-lp-not-N}, we have
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
         &\mspace{20mu} \norm{\Ebig{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi Q}}_1 \\ 
         \nonumber
         &=   \EBig{ \norm{\Ebig{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi Q  \,\big|\, \Sigma_t}}_1 \indibrac{D^{\textup{OL}}_t \neq [N]} }  \\
         \label{eq:two-set:steins-diff-expect-ell1-bound}
         &\leq 2\lambda_{Q} \Prob{D^{\textup{OL}}_t \neq [N]}.
    \end{align}

    Plugging \eqref{eq:two-set:steins-diff-expect-ell1-bound} into \eqref{eq:two-set:state-diff-steins-diff}, we get 
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
        \normbig{\Ebig{X_\infty([N]) - \mu^*} }_1 
        &\leq \lim_{T\to\infty} \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \norm{\Ebig{(X_{t+1}([N])-\mu^*)Q - (X_t([N])-\mu^*)\Phi Q}} \\
         \label{eq:two-set:state-diff-expect-prob-bound}
        &\leq 2\lambda_{Q} \Prob{D^{\textup{OL}}_\infty \neq [N]}.
    \end{align}
    where the expectations or probabilities of variables or events with subscript $\infty$ are shorthands for the long-run time averages. 

    Now we start to bound the optimality gap. We first rewrite the long-run average reward $R(\pi, \ve{S}_0)$ in terms of an expectation with respect to the states:  
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
        R(\pi, \ve{S}_0) 
        &= \Ebig{r(\ve{S}_\infty, \ve{A}_\infty)} 
        =  \E{r^\pi(X_\infty, D^{\textup{OL}}_\infty, D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_\infty)}, 
    \end{align}
    where $r^\pi(x, D^{\textup{OL}}, D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}})$ is the expected reward at a given state under the two-set policy: 
    \[
        r^\pi(x, D^{\textup{OL}}, D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}) \triangleq \Ebig{r(\ve{S}_t, \ve{A}_t) \,\big|\, X_t = x, D^{\textup{OL}}_t = D^{\textup{OL}}, D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t = D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}}. 
    \]
    Note that the RHS of $r^\pi(x, D^{\textup{OL}}, D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}})$'s definition does not depend on $t$ because the two-set policy is stationary and Markovian policy with state $(X_t, D^{\textup{OL}}_t, D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t)$. 

    Next, we examine the value of $r^\pi(x, D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}, D^{\textup{OL}})$ when $D^{\textup{OL}} = [N]$ and $D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}} = \emptyset$. Let $Y_t(s,a)$ be the random variable representing the fraction of arms in state $s$ taking action $a$ at time $t$. Then
    \begin{align*}
        r^\pi(X_t, [N], \emptyset) 
        &= \sum_{s\in\mathbb{S}, a\in\mathbb{A}} r(s,a) \Ebig{Y_t(s,a) \,\big|\, X_t, D^{\textup{OL}}_t = [N], D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t = \emptyset}. 
    \end{align*}
    By the definition of Optimal Local Control, 
    \begin{align}
        \Ebig{Y_t(s,a) \,\big|\, X_t, D^{\textup{OL}}_t = [N], D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t = \emptyset} &= {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(a|s) X_t([N], s) \quad s\neq \tilde{s} \\ 
        \Ebig{Y_t(\tilde{s},1) \,\big|\, X_t, D^{\textup{OL}}_t = [N], D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t = \emptyset, } &= \alpha - \sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}} {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s) X_t([N], s)  \\
        \Ebig{Y_t(\tilde{s},0) \,\big|\, X_t, D^{\textup{OL}}_t = [N], D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_t = \emptyset, } &= 1 - \alpha - \sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}} {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(0|s) X_t([N], s). 
    \end{align} 
    Therefore,
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:lp-priority-inst-reward}
        \begin{aligned}
        r^\pi(X_t, [N], \emptyset) 
        &= \sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}, a\in\mathbb{A}} \big(r(s,a) - r(\tilde{s},a)\big) {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(a|s) X_t([N],s) \\
        &\mspace{20mu} + \alpha r(\tilde{s},1) + (1-\alpha) r(\tilde{s},0),
        \end{aligned}
    \end{equation}
    Let $\hat{r}(v)$ be the affine function on $\Delta(\mathbb{S})$ such that $\hat{r}(X_t([N])) = r^\pi(X_t, \emptyset, [N])$: 
    \[
        \hat{r}(v) \triangleq \sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}, a\in\mathbb{A}} \big(r(s,a) - r(\tilde{s},a)\big) {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(a|s) v(s) + \alpha r(\tilde{s},1) + (1-\alpha) r(\tilde{s},0). 
    \]
    It is easy to see that $\hat{r}(v)$ is $4r_{\max}$-Lipschitz continuous with respect to $L_1$-norm, and $\hat{r}(\mu^*) = R^{\textup{rel}}$. 


    With the above definitions, we can lower bound $R(\pi, \ve{S}_0)$ as
    \begin{align*}
        R(\pi, \ve{S}_0) 
        &= \Ebig{r^\pi(X_\infty, D^{\textup{OL}}_\infty, D^{{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}}_\infty)}   \\
        &\geq \Ebig{ \hat{r}(X_\infty([N])) \indibrac{D^{\textup{OL}}_\infty = [N]}} - r_{\max} \Probbig{D^{\textup{OL}}_\infty \neq [N]} \\
        &= \Ebig{ \hat{r}(X_\infty([N]))}  - 2r_{\max} \Probbig{D^{\textup{OL}}_\infty \neq [N]} \\
        &= \hat{r}\big(\Ebig{X_\infty([N])}\big) - 2r_{\max} \Probbig{D^{\textup{OL}}_\infty \neq [N]} \\
        &= \hat{r}(\mu^*) + \hat{r}\big(\Ebig{X_\infty([N])}\big) - \hat{r}\big(\mu^*\big)   - 2r_{\max} \Probbig{D^{\textup{OL}}_\infty \neq [N]} \\
        &\geq  R^{\textup{rel}} - 4r_{\max} \norm{\Ebig{X_\infty([N]) - \mu^*}}_1 - 2r_{\max} \Probbig{D^{\textup{OL}}_\infty \neq [N]} \\
        &\geq R^{\textup{rel}} - 2r_{\max}(4 \lambda_{Q} + 1) \Probbig{D^{\textup{OL}}_t \neq [N]}. 
    \end{align*}
    Because $2r_{\max}(4 \lambda_{Q} + 1) = O(1)$, we have $R^{\textup{rel}} - R(\pi, \ve{S}_0) \leq O(1) \cdot  \Probbig{D^{\textup{OL}}_t \neq [N]}$.

Then r^pi(X_t, [N], emptyset) &= sum_sinS, ainA r(s,a) EbigY_t(s,a) \,big|\, X_t, D^textupOL_t = [N], D^sysbarpi^*_t = emptyset. By the definition of Optimal Local Control, EbigY_t(s,a) \,big|\, X_t, D^textupOL_t = [N], D^sysbarpi^*_t = emptyset &= sysbarpi^*(a|s) X_t([N], s) sneq tildes \\ EbigY_t(tildes,1) \,big|\, X_t, D^textupOL_t = [N], D^sysbarpi^*_t = emptyset, &= alpha - sum_sneq tildes sysbarpi^*(1|s) X_t([N], s) \\ EbigY_t(tildes,0) \,big|\, X_t, D^textupOL_t = [N], D^sysbarpi^*_t = emptyset, &= 1 - alpha - sum_sneq tildes sysbarpi^*(0|s) X_t([N], s). Therefore, r^pi(X_t, [N], emptyset) &= sum_sneq tildes, ainA big(r(s,a) - r(tildes,a)big) sysbarpi^*(a|s) X_t([N],s) \\ &mspace20mu + alpha r(tildes,1) + (1-alpha) r(tildes,0), Let hatr(v) be the affine function on Delta(S) such that hatr(X_t([N])) = r^pi(X_t, emptyset, [N]): \[ hatr(v) triangleq sum_sneq tildes, ainA big(r(s,a) - r(tildes,a)big) sysbarpi^*(a|s) v(s) + alpha r(tildes,1) + (1-alpha) r(tildes,0). \] It is easy to see that hatr(v) is 4r_max-Lipschitz continuous with respect to L_1-norm, and hatr(mu^*) = R^textuprel. With the above definitions, we can lower bound R(pi, veS_0) as R(pi, veS_0) &= Ebigr^pi(X_infty, D^textupOL_infty, D^sysbarpi^*_infty) \\ &geq Ebig hatr(X_infty([N])) indibracD^textupOL_infty = [N] - r_max ProbbigD^textupOL_infty neq [N] \\ &= Ebig hatr(X_infty([N])) - 2r_max ProbbigD^textupOL_infty neq [N] \\ &= hatrbig(EbigX_infty([N])big) - 2r_max ProbbigD^textupOL_infty neq [N] \\ &= hatr(mu^*) + hatrbig(EbigX_infty([N])big) - hatrbig(mu^*big) - 2r_max ProbbigD^textupOL_infty neq [N] \\ &geq R^textuprel - 4r_max normEbigX_infty([N]) - mu^*_1 - 2r_max ProbbigD^textupOL_infty neq [N] \\ &geq R^textuprel - 2r_max(4 lambda_Q + 1) ProbbigD^textupOL_t neq [N]. Because 2r_max(4 lambda_Q + 1) = O(1), we have R^textuprel - R(pi, veS_0) leq O(1) cdot ProbbigD^textupOL_t neq [N].

Let $f(a) = (a-\overline{\eta}/2)^+$. 
    To obtain an bound on $\Prob{V(\Sigma_\infty) > \overline{\eta}}$, we will calculate $\E{f(V(\Sigma_{t+1}))} - \E{f(V(\Sigma_{t}))}$ for each time step $t$ and invoking the fact that 
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:bar}
        \lim_{T\to\infty} \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \big(\E{f(V(\Sigma_{t+1}))} - \E{f(V(\Sigma_{t}))}\big) = 0.
    \end{equation}

    We will bound $\E{f(V(\Sigma_{t+1}))} - \E{f(V(\Sigma_{t}))}$ in three cases,  $V(\Sigma_{t}) > \overline{\eta}$, $\overline{\eta}/2 < V(\Sigma_{t}) \leq \overline{\eta}$, and  $V(\Sigma_{t}) \leq \overline{\eta}/2$. 

    First, if $V(\Sigma_{t}) > \overline{\eta}$, 
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
        &\mspace{20mu} \Ebig{f(V(\Sigma_{t+1})) \,\big|\, \Sigma_t} - f(V(\Sigma_t)) \\
        \nonumber
        &= \Ebig{\big(V(\Sigma_{t+1}) - V(\Sigma_t)\big)\indibrac{V(\Sigma_{t+1}) > V(\Sigma_t)} \,\big|\, \Sigma_t}  \\
        \nonumber
        &\mspace{20mu} + \Ebig{\big(V(\Sigma_{t+1}) - V(\Sigma_t)\big) \indibrac{\overline{\eta}/2 < V(\Sigma_{t+1}) \leq V(\Sigma_t)} \,\big|\, \Sigma_t}  \\
        \nonumber
        &\mspace{20mu} + \Ebig{\big(\overline{\eta}/2 - V(\Sigma_t)\big) \indibrac{V(\Sigma_{t+1}) \leq \overline{\eta}/2} \,\big|\, \Sigma_t}  \\
        \nonumber
        &\leq \Ebig{\big(V(\Sigma_{t+1}) - V(\Sigma_t)\big)\indibrac{V(\Sigma_{t+1}) > V(\Sigma_t)} \,\big|\, \Sigma_t}  \\
        \label{eq:two-set:drift-lem:interm-1}
        &\mspace{20mu} + \frac{1}{2} \Ebig{\big(V(\Sigma_{t+1}) - V(\Sigma_t)\big) \indibrac{ V(\Sigma_{t+1}) \leq V(\Sigma_t)} \,\big|\, \Sigma_t}  \\
        &= \frac{1}{2}\Ebig{\big(V(\Sigma_{t+1}) - V(\Sigma_t)\big)^+ \,\big|\, \Sigma_t}  + \frac{1}{2} \Ebig{V(\Sigma_{t+1}) - V(\Sigma_t) \,\big|\, \Sigma_t} \\
        \label{eq:two-set:drift-lem:interm-2}
        &\leq -\frac{1}{2}\gamma  + O(1/\sqrt{N}).
    \end{align}
    where the inequality in \eqref{eq:two-set:drift-lem:interm-1} follows uses the fact that when $V(\Sigma_{t}) \geq \overline{\eta}$, $V(\Sigma_{t+1}) \geq 0$, 
    \[
        \frac{1}{2}\big(V(\Sigma_{t+1}) - V(\Sigma_t)\big) - (\overline{\eta}/2 - V(\Sigma_t)) = \frac{1}{2}\big(V(\Sigma_{t+1}) + V(\Sigma_t)\big) - \overline{\eta}/2 \geq 0;
    \]
    the inequality in \eqref{eq:two-set:drift-lem:interm-2} applies the properties of $V$ assumed in \eqref{eq:two-set:drift-lem:drift-1} and \eqref{eq:two-set:drift-lem:jump-1}. 

    Next, consider the case of $\overline{\eta}/2 < V(\Sigma_{t}) \leq \overline{\eta}$.
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
         &\mspace{20mu} \Ebig{f(V(\Sigma_{t+1})) \,\big|\, \Sigma_t} - f(V(\Sigma_t)) \\ 
         \nonumber
        &\leq  \Ebig{\big(f(V(\Sigma_{t+1})) - f(V(\Sigma_t))\big) \indibrac{V(\Sigma_{t+1}) > V(\Sigma_t)} \,\big|\, \Sigma_t}  \\
        \nonumber
        &=  \Ebig{\big(V(\Sigma_{t+1}) - V(\Sigma_t)\big)^+ \,\big|\, \Sigma_t} \\
        \label{eq:two-set:drift-lem:interm-3}
        &= O(\exp(-C N)),
    \end{align}
    where \eqref{eq:two-set:drift-lem:interm-3} follows from \eqref{eq:two-set:drift-lem:jump-2}. 

    Finally, consider the case of $V(\Sigma_{t}) \leq \overline{\eta}/2$.
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
         &\mspace{20mu} \Ebig{f(V(\Sigma_{t+1})) \,\big|\, \Sigma_t} - f(V(\Sigma_t)) \\ 
         \nonumber
         &= \Ebig{(V(\Sigma_{t+1})-\overline{\eta}/2)^+ \,\big|\, \Sigma_t} \\
         \nonumber

We construct the subset $D_t$ by removing a suitable subset of arms from $[N]$. 
    We first remove each arm $i$ with state $S_t(i)\in S^+$ and $A_t(i) = 0$ or $S_t(i) \in S^-$ and $A_t(i) = 1$. After this step, we get a subset $D'$ with $N(1-d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t))$ arms. The budget usage of $D'$ equals $\alpha N - N \sum_{s\in S^-} Y_t(s,1)$. 
    Then $D_t$ is obtained by removing arms that take action $1$ or action $0$ from $D'$ such that the budget usage of $D_t$ equals $\floor{\alpha |D_t|}$.
    If $\alpha N - N \sum_{s\in S^-} Y_t(s,1)  > \alpha |D'|$, it is not hard to show that the number of arms removed from $D'$ is bounded by 
    \[
        |D'| - |D_t|  \leq \frac{1}{1-\alpha} \Big(\absbig{\alpha N - N \sum_{s\in S^-} Y_t(s,1) - \alpha |D'| }  + 1\Big) \leq  \frac{1}{1-\alpha} \big(Nd_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t) + 1\big); 
    \]
    If $\alpha N - N \sum_{s\in S^-} Y_t(s,1)  > \alpha |D'|$, it is not hard to show that the number of arms removed from $D'$ is bounded by 
    \[
         |D'| - |D_t| \leq \frac{1}{\alpha} \Big(\absbig{\alpha N - N \sum_{s\in S^-} Y_t(s,1) - \alpha |D'|}  + 1\Big) \leq  \frac{1}{\alpha} \big(Nd_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t) + 1\big).
    \]
    In both cases, we have 
    \begin{equation}
        |D'| - |D_t|  \leq \frac{1}{\beta}\big(Nd_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t) + 1\big),
    \end{equation}
    where recall that $\beta = \min(\alpha, 1-\alpha)$. 
    Now we get a subset $D_t$ such that $m(D_t) \geq 1 - d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t)- (d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t)+ 1/N) / \beta \geq 1-2d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t)/\beta - 1/(\beta N)$. Moreover, for each $i\in D_t$, $A_t(i) = 1$ if $S_t(i) \in S^+$; $A_t(i) = 0$ if $S_t(i) \in S^-$; the total budget usage of $D_t$ equals $\floor{\alpha |D_t|}$. 

    Following similar calculations as the proof of \Cref{lem:lp-priority-and-phi}, we can show that 
    \[
        \E{X_{t+1}(D_t) \,|\, X_t, \ve{A}_t} 
        = X_t(D_t) \Big(P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*} - c_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}^\top \big(P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})\big) \Big) + m(D_t) \frac{\floor{\alpha N}}{N} (P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})).
    \]
    whereas by the definition of $\Phi$,  
    \[
        (X_t(D_t) - m(D_t)\mu^*) \Phi + m(D_t) \mu^* = X_t(D_t) \Big(P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*} - c_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}^\top \big(P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})\big) \Big) + m(D_t) \alpha (P_1(\tilde{s}) - P_0(\tilde{s})).
    \]
    Comparing the above two equations, we get \eqref{eq:subset-lp-priority}.

    To show \eqref{eq:subset-lp-priority-as}, note that if we resample the actions using the Optimal Local Control for the arms in $D_t$,

\label{lem:hus-drift}
    Consider an instance of regular unstable RBs (\Cref{def:regular-unstable}). Let $K_1$ be any positive constant. Under any policy $\pi$, for any time step $t$, we have
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
          &\mspace{23mu} \Ebig{h_{+}(X_{t+1}, [N]) \,\big|\, \,\big|\, X_t, \ve{A}_t} - h_{+}(X_t, [N])\\
          &\geq 
         \frac{\epsilon_1 K_1- (2+\epsilon_1 + \epsilon_2) K_1 \indibrac{\mathcal{E}_t^c}}{\sqrt{N}} - \frac{6\lambda_{+}^{1/2}}{\beta N} -  \frac{8 \lambda_{+}^{1/2} d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t)}{\beta} \quad a.s., 
    \end{align}
    where $\beta = \min(\alpha, 1-\alpha)$; the event $\mathcal{E}_t$ is given by 
    \[
        \mathcal{E}_t = \Big\{h_{+}(X_t, [N]) > \frac{K_1}{\sqrt{N}} + \frac{2\lambda_{+}^{1/2} d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t)}{\beta} + \frac{\lambda_{+}^{1/2}}{\beta N}, \, \norm{X_t([N]) - \mu^*}_1 \leq \eta' -  \frac{6d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t)}{\beta} - \frac{3}{\beta N}\Big\},
    \]
    and $K_1 = \lambda_{+}^{1/2} K_{\textup{noise}} / (2+\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)$.

    By \Cref{lem:exist-subset-lp-priority}, there exists a coupling such that $\norm{X_{t+1}'(D_t) - X_{t+1}(D_t)}_1 \leq 2/N$ almost surely. 
    By the definition of $h_{-}$ and the fact that $m(D_t) \geq 1-2d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t) / \beta - 1/(\beta N)$, we have
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
        &\mspace{23mu} \Ebig{h_{-}(X_{t+1}, [N]) \,\big|\, X_t, \ve{A}_t} - (1-\epsilon_3) h_{-}(X_t, [N])  \\
        \nonumber
        &\leq  \Ebig{h_{-}(X_{t+1}, D_t) \,\big|\, X_t, \ve{A}_t} - (1-\epsilon_3) h_{-}(X_t, D_t) + 4\lambda_{-}^{1/2} (1-m(D_t))  \\
        \nonumber
        &\leq  \Ebig{h_{-}(X_{t+1}, D_t) \,\big|\, X_t, \ve{A}_t} - (1-\epsilon_3) h_{-}(X_t, D_t) + 8 \lambda_{-}^{1/2} d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t) / \beta + 4\lambda_{-}^{1/2} / (\beta N) \\
        \label{eq:pf-hst-drift:interm-1}
        &\leq \Ebig{h_{-}(X_{t+1}', D_t) \,\big|\, X_t, \ve{A}_t} - (1-\epsilon_3) h_{-}(X_t, D_t) + 8 \lambda_{-}^{1/2} d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t) / \beta + 6 \lambda_{-}^{1/2} /(\beta N).

For any system state $x$ and subset $D\subseteq [N]$, 
    define
    \[
        h_{\textup{lb}}(x, D) = L_{\textup{lb}} h_{+}(x, D) - h_{-}(x, D),
    \]
    where $L_{\textup{lb}} = 2\lambda_{-}^{1/2}|\mathbb{S}| / \epsilon_1$. 
    We will show that with an appropriate $L_{\textup{lb}}$ and for $N$ larger than a constant threshold, we have
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:pf-thm3:goal}
        \E{h_{\textup{lb}}(X_{t+1}, [N])} - \E{h_{\textup{lb}}(X_{t}, [N])}
        \geq \Omega\Big(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\Big) - \Theta(1)\cdot \E{d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t)}  \quad \forall t\geq 0.
    \end{align}
    If we can prove \eqref{eq:pf-thm3:goal}, then taking the long-run average on two sides of the inequality implies 
    \begin{equation*}
        0 = \E{h_{\textup{lb}}(X_{\infty}, [N])} - \E{h_{\textup{lb}}(X_{\infty}, [N])} \geq \Omega\Big(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\Big) - \Theta(1)\cdot \E{d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_\infty)},
    \end{equation*}
    so $\E{d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_\infty)} = \Omega(1/\sqrt{N})$. Combined with \Cref{lem:opt-gap-linear-comp}, we get $R^{\textup{rel}} - R(\pi, \ve{S}_0) = \Omega(1/\sqrt{N})$, which proves \Cref{thm:instability-lower-bound}. 

    Now we prove \eqref{eq:pf-thm3:goal} using the formulas of $h_{+}(X_t, [N])$ and $h_{-}(X_t, [N])$'s drifts given in \Cref{lem:hus-drift} and \Cref{lem:hst-drift}. 
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
        &\mspace{23mu} \E{h_{\textup{lb}}(X_{t+1}, [N]) \,\big|\, X_t, \ve{A}_t} - h_{\textup{lb}}(X_{t}, [N]) \\
        \nonumber
        &= L_{\textup{lb}} \Big(\Ebig{h_{+}(X_{t+1}, [N]) \,\big|\, X_t, \ve{A}_t} - h_{+}(X_t, [N])\Big) - \Big( \Ebig{h_{-}(X_{t+1}, [N]) \,\big|\, X_t, \ve{A}_t} - h_{-}(X_t, [N]) \Big) \\
        \nonumber
        &\geq L_{\textup{lb}} \Big( \frac{\epsilon_1 K_1- (2+\epsilon_1 + \epsilon_2) K_1 \indibrac{\mathcal{E}_t^c}}{\sqrt{N}} - \frac{6\lambda_{+}^{1/2}}{\beta N} -  8 \lambda_{+}^{1/2} \beta^{-1} d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t) \Big)  \\
        \nonumber
        &\mspace{20mu}
        + \epsilon_3 h_{-}(X_t, [N]) - \frac{\lambda_{-}^{1/2}|\mathbb{S}|}{\sqrt{N}} - \frac{10\lambda_{-}^{1/2}|\mathbb{S}|}{\beta N} - 8\lambda_{-}^{1/2} \beta^{-1} d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t) \\
        \label{eq:pf-thm3:interm-2}
        &= \Big(L_{\textup{lb}} \epsilon_1 K_1 - \lambda_{-}^{1/2}|\mathbb{S}|\Big)\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}} + \Big(\epsilon_3 h_{-}(X_t, [N]) - \frac{L_{\textup{lb}}(2+\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)K_1}{\sqrt{N}} \indibrac{\mathcal{E}_t^c} \Big) \\
        \label{eq:pf-thm3:interm-3}
        &\mspace{20mu} - \big(8L_{\textup{lb}} \lambda_{+}^{1/2} + 8\lambda_{-}^{1/2}\big)\beta^{-1} d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t)  - O\Big(\frac{1}{N}\Big).
    \end{align}
    Note that the coefficient of the $1/\sqrt{N}$ in  \eqref{eq:pf-thm3:interm-2} equals $\lambda_{-}^{1/2}|\mathbb{S}|$, which is positive. 
    
    Comparing \eqref{eq:pf-thm3:interm-2}-\eqref{eq:pf-thm3:interm-3} with our goal, \eqref{eq:pf-thm3:goal}, it remains to lower bound the second term in \eqref{eq:pf-thm3:interm-2}. 
    First, observe that given the event $\mathcal{E}_t$, the second term of \eqref{eq:pf-thm3:interm-2} is non-negative. So we only need to consider the event $\mathcal{E}_t^c$. 
    By definition, $\mathcal{E}_t^c$ implies that 
    \begin{align*}
        h_{+}(X_t, [N]) &\leq \frac{K_1}{\sqrt{N}} + \frac{2\lambda_{+}^{1/2} d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t)}{\beta} + \frac{\lambda_{+}^{1/2}}{\beta N}, \\
        \norm{X_t([N]) - \mu^*}_1 &> \eta' -  \frac{6d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t)}{\beta} - \frac{3}{\beta N}.
    \end{align*}
    By \eqref{eq:Uus-plus-Ust-strength} in \Cref{lem:uus-ust-properties}, 
    \[
        h_{+}(X_t, [N]) + h_{-}(X_t, [N]) \geq K_{\textup{norm}} \norm{X_t([N]) - \mu^*}_1,
    \]
    so given $\mathcal{E}_t^c$, 
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
        h_{-}(X_t, [N]) 
        &\geq K_{\textup{norm}} \norm{X_t([N]) - \mu^*}_1 - h_{+}(X_t, [N]) \\
        \nonumber
        &\geq K_{\textup{norm}}\Big(\eta' -  \frac{6d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t)}{\beta} - \frac{3}{\beta N}\Big) -  \frac{K_1}{\sqrt{N}} - \frac{2\lambda_{+}^{1/2} d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t)}{\beta} - \frac{\lambda_{+}^{1/2}}{\beta N} \\
        \nonumber
        &= K_{\textup{norm}} \eta' - \frac{K_1}{\sqrt{N}} - \big(6K_{\textup{norm}} + 2\lambda_{+}^{1/2}\big)\beta^{-1} d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t) - O\Big(\frac{1}{N}\Big).
    \end{align}
    Therefore, given $\mathcal{E}_t^c$, combining the above lower bound, if $N \geq K_1^2 \big(\epsilon_3+L_{\textup{lb}}(2+\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)\big)^2 / (K_{\textup{norm}}\eta'\epsilon_3)^2$, 
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
        &\mspace{23mu} \epsilon_3 h_{-}(X_t, [N])  - \frac{L_{\textup{lb}}(2+\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)K_1}{\sqrt{N}} \indibrac{\mathcal{E}_t^c} \\
        \nonumber
        &\geq \epsilon_3 K_{\textup{norm}} \eta'  - \frac{K_1\big(\epsilon_3 + L_{\textup{lb}}(2+\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)\big)}{\sqrt{N}} - \epsilon_3\big( 6K_{\textup{norm}} + 2\lambda_{+}^{1/2} \big) \beta^{-1} d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t) - O\Big(\frac{1}{N}\Big), \\
        \label{eq:pf-thm3:interm-4}
        &\geq  - \epsilon_3 \big( 6K_{\textup{norm}} + 2\lambda_{+}^{1/2} \big) \beta^{-1} d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t) - O\Big(\frac{1}{N}\Big).
    \end{align}

    Substituting \eqref{eq:pf-thm3:interm-4} back to the second term of  \eqref{eq:pf-thm3:interm-2}, we get 
    \begin{align}
        \nonumber
        &\mspace{23mu} \E{h_{\textup{lb}}(X_{t+1}, [N]) \,\big|\, X_t, \ve{A}_t} - h_{\textup{lb}}(X_{t}, [N]) \\
        \nonumber
        &\geq \frac{\lambda_{-}^{1/2}|\mathbb{S}|}{\sqrt{N}} - \big(6\epsilon_3 K_{\textup{norm}} + 2\epsilon_3\lambda_{+}^{1/2} + 8L_{\textup{lb}} \lambda_{+}^{1/2} + 8\lambda_{-}^{1/2} \big) \beta^{-1} d_{\textup{IC}}(Y_t) - O\Big(\frac{1}{N}\Big),
    \end{align}
    which implies \eqref{eq:pf-thm3:goal} and finishes the proof.

nodes.statement: Throughout this proof, we fix X_t and A_t and omit them in the conditioning when writing expectations or probabilities. Recalling the statement of Property , it suffices to show that for any xi in R^|S| with normplainxi_2 = 1 and mu^* xi^top = 0, there exists a constant K_textupnoise > 0 such that for any N larger than a constant and any time step t, if the local optimal policy is applicable, we have Ebigabsbigbig(X_t+1([N]) - mu^* - (X_t([N]) - mu^*)Phi big) xi^top \,big|\, X_t, veA_t geq fracK_textupnoisesqrtN, where veA_t follows the Optimal Local Control. Note that in this case, the parameter eta' in Property of Crefdef:regular-unstable could be any positive number such that normX_t([N]) - mu^*_1 leq eta' guarantees the condition for applying the Optimal Local Control. We first show that for any xi in R^|S| such that normxi_2 = 1 and mu^* xi^top = 0, xi_max - xi_min geq 1/sqrt|S|. where xi_max = max_sinS xi(s) and xi_min = min_sinS xi(s). Observe that we must have either xi_max geq 1/sqrt|S| or xi_min geq - 1/sqrt|S|, because otherwise normxi_2 < 1. We first show for the case with xi_max geq 1/sqrt|S|. In this case, we must have xi_min leq 1/sqrt|S|, because otherwise normxi_2 > 1. Let mathbbm1_textupscaled in R^|S| be the whose entries are all 1/sqrt|S|. Then \[ normxi -mathbbm1_textupscaled_infty leq maxbig(xi_max - 1/sqrt|S|, 1/sqrt|S| - xi_minbig) leq xi_max - xi_min. \] On the other hand, because normmu^*_1 = 1 and mu^* mathbbm1_textupscaled^top = 1/sqrt|S|, \[ normxi - mathbbm1_textupscaled_infty geq mu^* mathbbm1_textupscaled^top - mu^* xi^top = 1/sqrt|S|. \] Combining the last two inequalities yields . For the case with xi_min leq -1/sqrt|S|, can be proved in an analogous way. To show , we invoke the Paley-Zygmund inequality to get nonumber &mspace23mu Probbig(X_t+1([N]) xi^top -EplainX_t+1([N]) xi^topbig)^2 > frac12VarX_t+1([N]) xi^top \\ &geq frac14 fracVarX_t+1([N]) xi^top^2Ebig(X_t+1([N]) xi^top -EplainX_t+1([N]) xi^topbig)^4. Next, we lower bound the second moment of X_t+1([N]) xi^top -EplainX_t+1([N]) xi^top in . For any timestep t, given X_t, veA_t, we have X_t+1([N]) xi^top &= sum_sinS X_t+1([N], s) xi(s) \\ &= frac1N sum_sinS sum_iin[N] indibracveS_t+1(i) = s xi(s) \\ &= frac1N sum_iin[N] xi(veS_t+1(i)). Note that conditioned on X_t, veA_t, xi(veS_t+1(i)) are independent across i. Therefore, the variance of X_t+1([N]) xi^top is given by \[ VarX_t+1([N]) xi^top = frac1N^2 sum_iin[N] Varxi(veS_t+1(i)). \] Because P(s,a,s') > 0 for all s,s'inS, ainA, the support of veS_t+1(i) is the whole state space S. Moreover, because xi_max - xi_min > 1/sqrt|S|, we have Varxi(veS_t+1(i)) &geq min_s,a,s' P(s,a,s') Big( (xi_max - Exi(veS_t+1(i)))^2 + (xi_min - Exi(veS_t+1(i)))^2 Big) \\ &geq frac12 min_s,a,s' P(s,a,s') (xi_max - xi_min)^2 \\ &geq fracmin_s,a,s' P(s,a,s')2|S|, where min_s,a,s' is a shorthand for min_s,s'inS, ainA. Therefore, VarX_t+1([N]) xi^top geq frac1N^2 sum_iin[N] Varxi(veS_t+1(i)) geq fracmin_s,a,s' P(s,a,s')2|S|N. Next, we upper bound the fourth moment of X_t+1([N]) xi^top -EplainX_t+1([N]) xi^top. Using the fact that X_t+1([N]) xi^top = sum_iin[N] xi(veS_t+1(i)) / N, we get nonumber &mspace23mu Ebig(X_t+1([N]) xi^top -EplainX_t+1([N]) xi^topbig)^4 \\ nonumber &= frac1N^4 Big( sum_iin[N] Ebig(xi(veS_t+1(i)) - Exi(veS_t+1(i)big)^4 + 6 sum_1leq i < j leq N Varxi(veS_t+1(i) Varxi(veS_t+1(j) Big) \\ nonumber &leq frac1N^4Big(N (xi_max - xi_min)^4 + 6 fracN(N-1)2 (xi_max - xi_min)^4 Big) \\ &leq frac3(xi_max-xi_min)^4N^2. Substituting the calculations in and back to , we get nonumber &mspace23mu Probbig(X_t+1([N]) xi^top -EplainX_t+1([N]) xi^topbig)^2 > fracmin_s,a,s' P(s,a,s')4|S|N \\ nonumber &geq Big(fracmin_s,a,s' P(s,a,s')2|S|NBig)^2 fracN^212(xi_max-xi_min)^4 \\ &= fracmin_s,a,s' P(s,a,s')^247|S|^2 (xi_max-xi_min)^4. Because under the Optimal Local Control, we have normEplainX_t+1([N]) \,|\, X_t, veA_t - EplainX_t+1([N]) xi^top \,|\, X_t leq 2/N and EplainX_t+1([N]) \,|\, X_t = X_t([N]) Phi, we can rewrite the bound to get \[ Probabsbigbig(X_t+1([N]) xi^top - X_t([N]) Phi big)xi^top > fracmin_s,a,s' P(s,a,s')^1/22|S|^1/2 sqrtN - frac2N geq fracmin_s,a,s' P(s,a,s')^247|S|^2 (xi_max-xi_min)^4. \] Therefore, Eabsbigbig(X_t+1([N]) xi^top - X_t([N]) Phi big)xi^top &geq Big(fracmin_s,a,s' P(s,a,s')^1/22|S|^1/2 sqrtN - frac2N Big)cdot fracmin_s,a,s' P(s,a,s')^247|S|^2 (xi_max-xi_min)^4, which implies with K_textupnoise being the coefficient of 1/sqrtN in the last expression.

We will verify that the example in Figure~1 of \cite{HonXieCheWan_23} is regular unstable. 
    
    In this example, the single-armed MDP $(\mathbb{S}, \mathbb{A}, P, r)$ is defined as below: $\mathbb{S} = \{1,2,3\}$; $\mathbb{A}=\{0,1\}$; the transition kernel $P$ is given by 
    \begin{align*}
    P( \cdot ,0,\cdot ) \ &=\ \begin{bmatrix}
    0.02232142 & 0.10229283 & 0.87538575\\
    0.03426605 & 0.17175704 & 0.79397691\\
    0.52324756 & 0.45523298 & 0.02151947
    \end{bmatrix}, \\
    P( \cdot ,1,\cdot ) \ &=\ \begin{bmatrix}
    0.14874601 & 0.30435809 & 0.54689589\\
    0.56845754 & 0.41117331 & 0.02036915\\
    0.25265570 & 0.27310439 & 0.4742399
    \end{bmatrix};
    \end{align*}
    The reward function $r$ is defined as
    \begin{align*}
        r( \cdot , 0) \ &=
        \ \begin{bmatrix}
            0 & 0 & 0
            \end{bmatrix}, \\
        r( \cdot , 1) \ &=
        \ \begin{bmatrix}
            0.37401552 & 0.11740814 & 0.07866135
            \end{bmatrix}.
    \end{align*}
    Let $\alpha = 0.4$ in the budget constraint. 
    The optimal solution of the LP-relaxation \eqref{eq:lp-single} is:
    \[
        y^*( \cdot ,\cdot ) \ =\ \begin{bmatrix}
            0 & 0.29943\\
            0.23768 & 0.10057\\
            0.36232 & 0
            \end{bmatrix},
    \]
    where the first column corresponds to $y^*(s,0)$ and the second column corresponds to $y^*(s, 1)$. 
    
    Since $P(s,a,s')> 0$ for all $s,a,s'$, $P_{{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}$ is an aperiodic unichain, so \Cref{assump:aperiodic-unichain} holds. Also, from $y^*$, we can see that the state $2$ is the unique neutral state, implying \Cref{assump:non-degeneracy}. 
    Moreover, one can numerically verify that $y^*$ is the unique solution to \eqref{eq:lp-single}, so Property \ref{assump:unique-and-communicating} of \Cref{def:regular-unstable} is satisfied; 
    the moduli of the eigenvalues of $\Phi$ are $\{1.133, 0, 0.059\}$, so Property \ref{assump:instability} of \Cref{def:regular-unstable} is satisfied. 
    
    Finally, observe that in this example, $P(s,a,s') > 0$ for any $s,s'\in\mathbb{S}$ and $a\in\mathbb{A}$. Therefore, we invoke the sufficient condition \Cref{lem:assump-6-helper} proved in \Cref{app:remark-noise-assumption} to conclude that this example satisfies Property \ref{assump:orthogonal-noise} of \Cref{def:regular-unstable}.

In this proof, we write $\epsilon_0 = (|S^{\emptyset}|+1) / N$ for simplicity. To get a contradiction, suppose \eqref{eq:lp-priority-condition-1-restate} does not hold, i.e.,
    \[
        \sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}} {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s) x(D, s) > \alpha m(D) - \epsilon_0.
    \]
    Let $p_{\max} = \max_{s\neq \tilde{s}} {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s)$. 
    Because \eqref{eq:solve-eta-1-begins}--\eqref{eq:solve-eta-1-ends} is feasible, we must have $p_{\max} \geq \alpha$. 
    We define the sets $S^a$ and $S^b$ to be
    \begin{align*}
        S^a &= \{s\in\mathbb{S}\colon s\neq \tilde{s}, {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s) = p_{\max}  \}\\
        S^b &=  \{s\in\mathbb{S} \colon s\neq \tilde{s}, {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s) < p_{\max}  \}.
    \end{align*}
    Now we construct a feasible $\ve{z}$ to the SOCP in \eqref{eq:solve-eta-1-begins}--\eqref{eq:solve-eta-1-ends} as
    \begin{equation}
        z(s) = 
        \begin{cases}
            (x(D, s) + c) / m(D)  \quad & \text{if } s\in S^a\\
            (x(D, s) - d)^+ / m(D) \quad & \text{if } s\in S^b\cup{\tilde{s}},
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    for some $d > 0$ to be determined later, and $c$ is such that $\sum_{s\in\mathbb{S}} z(s) = 1$. Note that such $c$ always exists for any $d$. 
    Observe that when $d$ is sufficiently large, $\sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}} {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s) \ve{z}(s) = p_{\max} \geq \alpha$. By the intermediate value theorem, we can let $d$ be such that $\sum_{s\neq \tilde{s}} {{\sysbar{\pi}}^*}(1|s) \ve{z}(s) = \alpha$. Then $\ve{z}$ is feasible to the SOCP in \eqref{eq:solve-eta-1-begins}--\eqref{eq:solve-eta-1-ends}. 
    Therefore, by the definition of $\eta$, we must have 
    \begin{equation}
        \norm{\ve{z} - \mu^*}_U \geq \eta. 
    \end{equation}

    To get a contradiction, we only need to show that 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:proposition-socp-fe:intermediate-goal}
        \norm{x(D) - m(D)\ve{z}}_U \leq \epsilon_N^{\text{fe}} = 2\sqrt{2}\lambda_U^{1/2} \epsilon_0,
    \end{equation}
    which would imply that 
    \begin{align*}
        \norm{x(D) - m(D)\mu^*}_U 
        &\geq \norm{m(D)\ve{z} - m(D)\mu^*}_U - \norm{x(D) - m(D)\ve{z}}_U \\
        &\geq \eta m(D) - \epsilon_N^{\text{fe}}.
    \end{align*}

    To show \eqref{eq:proposition-socp-fe:intermediate-goal}, observe that 
    \begin{align*}
